entries.name: Stokely Carmichael

expected.charges: Breach of peace (Freedom Rides; refusing to leave segregated facilities)
expected.sentence:
49 days at Mississippi State Penitentiary (Parchman); first of more than 30 civil-rights-era arrests

Verdict as recorded: Yes — Mississippi state court, 1961

updates.sentence: Arrested and jailed in Jackson on June 8, 1961 during the Freedom Rides; subsequently held at Parchman. Released in 1961. Published accounts differ between 49 and 53 days in custody. Neither a precise release date nor a reconciled exact time-served total is established by the sources reviewed here. The previous June 3 arrest and July 22 release are not supported by the archival arrest record.

entries.rationale: Archive mugshot metadata and historian Peniel Joseph establish June8 arrest. Conflicting49/53day accounts cannot establish an exact release; preserve release year1961 and remove false exact counter.

entries.name: Hank Adams

expected.charges: Illegal fishing in violation of Washington state regulations (multiple counts) — 1968-1971 treaty-rights fish-ins

updates.charges: Fishing-rights protest arrest during the September 1968 Nisqually River fish-ins.
updates.sentence: Arrested during the first days of the September 1968 fish-in campaign and released on bail by September 13, 1968. The exact arrest and bail-release days, and the eventual disposition of this individual arrest, remain unresolved. He faced other fishing-rights arrests between 1968 and 1971; those are not represented as one continuous term. A separate 30-day sentence beginning in January 1972 is documented in the Washington Secretary of State biography.

entries.rationale: UW cites September9 and13,1968 contemporary Seattle Times reports establishing arrest and bail within September. Replace unsupportedDecember31,1969 chronology with the identified documented episode; do not turn bail-by13 into an exact release.1972term requires separate case.
